subject: Human Evolution
title: Fruit Beginnings
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Fruit Beginnings.

hook.text: Our earliest primate ancestors lived in trees and ate mostly fruit. That sweet tooth still controls you.

buildup.text: Tropical forests offered year-round fruit. Color vision evolved specifically to spot ripe ones.

discovery.text: Primates that found ripe fruit faster got more calories and out-reproduced their competitors.

twist.text: When forests shrank, fruit became scarce. Species stuck on fruit diets went extinct or stayed in trees.

climax.text: Our ancestors survived because they could switch to tougher foods: roots, seeds, and eventually meat.

punchline.text: Leaving fruit behind let us leave the trees.

quiz.question: Why did early primates evolve color vision?
options: To identify ripe fruit more efficiently
